title: 3D-lowey Scene Script v3
description: Actions that speak relations, not coordinates: add from the Kit, place by relation (grounded, apart), frame shots, light by recipe, animate by intent. One script = one Proposal = one undo step. v1/v2 scripts upgrade on the way in. Short reference: GET /v2/actions (LoweyCore ScriptReference).

properties.description: Known keys: position, rotation, scale, visible, locked, opacity, stepping (inherit|ones|twos|threes), color, emissive, emissiveIntensity, roughness, metallic, shading, castsShadow, lightColor, lightIntensity, lightRange, spotAngle, lightShadows, fieldOfView, focusDistance, aperture, portraitZoom, portraitShift, seed

oneOf.description: cubic bezier x1, y1, x2, y2

easing.description: Shapes the segment leaving this key.

items.description: kind.type: followPath | lookAt | follow | orbit | noise | windSway | bob | spin
Insert or replace a track; omit `track` to remove it.

time.description: Seconds, a keyword, a spoken word or a marker.

then.description: A Kit/library model ("asset": an id like kit.office-desk, or words), a shape, or a group; optionally placed by relation.

M12: the app around the scene, not an edit (nothing to undo): the hand's tool, a panel, play, pause, the playhead, undo and redo, present, notes, the timeline, the director's view, the interface, framing the selection, flying, what's shown, the selection, an export into the project's renders (fetched from /v1/renders), the AR view, a Monitor window.
Copies in a line or ring.
A Blob character (a likeness or a recipe).
Combines shapes into the target (it keeps its name, look and place; the others are used up): subtract cuts wheel arches and windows, union joins, intersect keeps the overlap.
A camera.
A camera move.
Captions on/off and style.

A humanoid puppet from a recipe; or, with "op", K1's character maker: "new" from a start (person, fourLegs, wings, blob, nothing), "adopt" (the target itself becomes the character, whole, keeping its own rig), "add" a part to a character or any thing (paired parts mirrored unless symmetric is false), "style" (another of the part's set), "remove", "assign" (a thing becomes a part, or the drawing of a face state), "state" (bend a face state: open, wide, round, smile, lift, tilt, close; or reset), "proportion" (by a factor or to metres), "say" (lip sync a typed line), "rig". Changes to parts rig it again in the same step.
A built-in clip.
A raw EditCommand.
Cut to a camera.

D1's motion design: an SVG logo stood up as solids (one a colour); copies of a thing in a grid, a circle, a line or along a path, moved by effects (random, delay, push) through fields (everywhere, near a point, a ripple); links that let a thing's motion or a sound (loudness, bass, beat) drive another thing; a morph into another thing's shape; letters that animate; and the loop check, which can close the loop.
Copies beside the originals (Edit ▸ Duplicate).
A screen effect; impact, focusLines and comicDots aim at a thing (target) or a point (center, 0…1 from the top left).
A face, from a moment on.

F1's film tools: a lens in millimetres on a camera body; the picture's shape; focus that follows a thing (a later one pulls focus); a rig (dolly, crane, orbit, handheld) with its moves keyed; haze and god rays; turning the HDRI; and the shots as a storyboard would list them.
Drawn FX from the library.
The camera solver: shot type and composition on a subject (a new camera when "camera" doesn't exist).
Group under a new parent.

G1's guest kits. Room: roofs over walls or an outline, columns, beams, railings, scale people, terrain, a name lying on the floor. Print: the best way up, a split with pegs, hollowing with drain holes, engraving or embossing text, ISO screw holes (M2-M10: clearance, counterbored, for a tap, threaded, a heat-set insert), a jar with a screw-on lid, bolts and nuts, scale to size. Study: explode a group (and back). Game: greybox pieces on a metre grid, freeze transforms.
Say what it should do; the app picks the animation.
Keyframes.
The timeline's length.
A light: a bulb (point), a spot, a sun, or a soft panel (a rectangle, "size" in metres) aimed at a thing.
A lighting recipe placed for the shot camera (replaces the recipe's earlier lamps).
Mouth shapes from the transcript.
The Look, mood and post; per-object Looks.
A timeline marker.

U6's modelling set on one thing: smooth, subdivide, smoothAngle, flat, bend, cage, brush, pull, loopCut, knife, fillHoles, mergeByDistance, cleanUp, linkedCopy, unlink, pivot, size; H1's steps (list) and step (change one).

A1's motion: a path the thing follows at the line's own timing ("times" from the first point, else a steady "speed" or a "duration"), facing the way it goes and leaning into turns (characters stay upright); following a drawn line; looking at a thing (a character turns its head; "from" switches the look at a moment); picking up and handing off ("by" a thing or a skeleton's "joint"), putting down, letting go; even speed, the timing of a whole motion, and turning its front.
U8's review notes: a pin on a thing (it follows the thing) or at a point, carried in the file and answered in place; list them, reply, resolve, reopen or delete one by its number or id.
A 2D overlay in frame space.

U7's texturing on one thing: a fill layer of a colour, a material or wear; a decal; whole faces; the layers; a mask; mirrored strokes; the texture's size; hand-marked seams; normals baked from a detailed copy; fur.
An emitter.

P1's physics: make things real (a material in words, how they move, their numbers), the scene's gravity, wind, ground and start, joints and mechanisms, forces (fan, pull, whirl) and fluids (pour, splash, smoke, fire), Keep it (the run becomes keys), Settle, does it stand, and the real sun of a place and date.
Place by relation (grounded, apart from what's there; left/right as seen from the reference's front).
A motion preset.
A sketch region made into a solid: pulled out of its plane (a negative distance cuts into the thing it was drawn on), swept along a path, revolved around an axis or lofted through others.
Tint with a palette slot.

Q1's Reference window over the stage (not an edit): open it, show the whole scene (canvas), a picture already in the project (image, named by /v2/media?as=reference) or the front camera (face); frame the whole scene again; close it.
Delete.
Rename.
Real-world size in metres.
Copies scattered.
A property (keyed when "at" is given).

Construction curves on a plane (xy facing front, xz the ground, yz the side, or an origin and a normal) or on the face of a thing; closed curves make the areas profile uses. Points are metres on the plane.
3D words; `font` names a font file brought into the project (fonts/…).
Words with known timings on a voiceover clip (a script, a laptop TTS).
Absolute transform (edge cases).

M12's web layer: a page (HTML, CSS and JavaScript: a three.js scene, an HTML animation timed to the clock), a Lottie file or a project file played on a screen in the scene or over the frame, sandboxed with no network, its clock stepped by the timeline (60 frames a second from `start`) so preview and export match; edit one, list them.
